title: New to Islam
hookLine: a man pulls back his hand at the pledge; Islam wipes out what came before, and every first Muslim was new

lines: A CONDITION: THAT I BE FORGIVEN.
cards: A man stands in front of the Prophet ﷺ to give his pledge. For years he's been on the other side. The Prophet stretches out his right hand, and the man pulls his own hand back.
What's wrong, Amr? I want a condition, he says. That I be forgiven.
Amr ibn al-As told this story himself, on his deathbed, and Sahih Muslim keeps it. The Prophet's answer is today's lesson, for anyone who's new. Today: shahada.

teach.h: ISLAM WIPES OUT WHAT CAME BEFORE.
teach.b: The answer was: don't you know that Islam wipes out what came before it? Whatever the past held, the pledge starts a clean page.
The shahada is the sentence that does it: there is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah.
Said with meaning, it's how a person becomes Muslim. Some say it in a mosque after Friday prayer, to a room that breaks into Allahu akbar. Some say it quietly with a friend.

People who take this step often call themselves converts, and many prefer reverts, from a hadith in Bukhari that every child is born on the fitrah, a natural sense of God. Becoming Muslim, in that picture, is coming back.
Then what? New Muslims often say the hardest part is the flood: a hundred rules on day one, Arabic from strangers, a new name suggested in the parking lot. The tradition's own pace is gentler.
Bukhari reports a man from Najd who asked the Prophet what Islam asks of him, and was told: the five prayers, the fast, zakat.

teach.h: NO MORE AND NO LESS: HE SUCCEEDED.
teach.b: He said: I'll do no more and no less. And the Prophet said: he has succeeded, if he's truthful.
Many scholars add that a new Muslim doesn't need to change a name with a good meaning, and that Arabic comes slowly, a line at a time. And a word to those already inside.
Every Muslim of the first generation was new. Khadijah, Abu Bakr, Bilal: each said the shahada for the first time, to a small community that made room for them.
Tomorrow's verse even sets aside a share of zakat for hearts being drawn close.

how: A person becomes Muslim by saying the shahada sincerely, often before witnesses at a mosque; many mosques run classes and mentoring for new Muslims, and teachers commonly advise learning the practices step by step.

o: the testimony of faith that makes someone Muslim
a year of study before joining a mosque
the new Arabic name given to a convert

games.q: you are Amr ibn al-As. the Prophet ﷺ holds out his hand for your pledge, and you pull yours back. why?
o: I want a condition: that I be forgiven.
games.why: he wanted forgiveness first, and was told: don't you know that Islam wipes out what came before it?

practice: Think back to a day you were new somewhere: a school, a job, a country, someone's family kitchen, and remember who made room for you, a name, a small kindness, a seat saved.
Then picture someone new in your world right now, at work, in a class, at a mosque, and picture being the one who makes room.

wordCard.voice: Shahada. The testimony: there is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah. Said with meaning, it's the first step, and the first pillar. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: testimony, witnessing, from a root meaning to be present and to see.

carryVoice: Your line: everyone started new. The first Muslims were all beginners, and every door has someone just walking through it. Day one hundred fifty-one, done.
